steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Common pop progressions: I-V-vi-IV (four-chord loop), I-IV-V (rock/blues), ii-V-I (jazz cadence) — each creates a different harmonic character.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Accompaniment styles define genre: Alberti bass (Classical), riff (rock/pop), broken chords (Romantic), ostinato (minimalist), pedal/drone (folk/traditional).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Harmonic rhythm (how often chords change) affects momentum: fast harmonic rhythm creates drive; slow harmonic rhythm creates stasis and calm.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Dominant seventh chords (V7) create tension that resolves to the tonic — they are essential for cadences and key-defining progressions.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how chords and accompaniment writing are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use chords and accompaniment writing. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use chords and accompaniment writing in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their | A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how chords and accompaniment writing are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comparativ | A practical application showing understanding of how chords and accompaniment writing can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended effect

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
